# Vim/Neovim Parity Scoreboard

Nevi aims for full Vim/Neovim keybind compatibility — and backs the claim with
tests instead of adjectives. This page is generated from the same inventories
the test suite enforces, so it cannot drift from what is actually verified.

## Summary

- **329 keybinds implemented** ([KEYBINDINGS.md](KEYBINDINGS.md)), **39 planned** ([KEYBINDS_ROADMAP.md](KEYBINDS_ROADMAP.md))
- **80 keybinds in the coverage inventory**, each mapped to the automated test that protects it:
  - 78 verified against real Neovim (v0.11.3) by the Vim oracle
  - 1 protected by focused Nevi regression tests
  - 1 covered as default-keymap plumbing with dedicated tests
- **241 oracle cases**: motions (121), editing (60), insert-entry (11), open-line (20), replace (27), undo-redo (2)
- **0 tracked coverage gaps**
- **112 of 428 documented keybind rows map to an inventoried keybind**; the rest work today but are not yet individually tracked ([full list below](#documented-but-not-yet-inventoried))

## How the Vim oracle works

Each oracle case is an initial buffer plus a literal key sequence. The keys are
replayed in Nevi and in `nvim --headless`, and the resulting buffer content,
cursor position, viewport top, and mode are compared. Cases run
deterministically in the normal test suite; CI additionally replays them
against a pinned real Neovim (v0.11.3) on macOS and Linux
(`NEVI_VIM_ORACLE=1`). A failure report includes both editors' snapshots.

The coverage inventory (`src/keybind_coverage.rs`) is itself enforced by tests:
entries must be unique and complete, oracle references must name real cases,
and any gap must carry an explicit written reason — a keybind cannot silently
claim protection.
